chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about jihad: Is it a sunnah or an obligation? So he said: Jihad is of four kinds — two are obligatory, and one is a sunnah that cannot be established except alongside the obligatory.

As for one of the two obligations, it is a man's striving against his own soul from the disobedience of God, Mighty and Majestic, and that is among the greatest jihads; and fighting those of the disbelievers who are nearest to you is an obligation.

As for the jihad that is a sunnah that cannot be established except alongside an obligation, fighting the enemy is obligatory upon the entire community, and if they were to abandon jihad, the punishment would certainly come upon them — this is among the punishments of the community; and it is a sunnah upon the Imam alone to go to the enemy with the community and fight them.

As for the jihad that is sunnah, it is every sunnah that a man establishes and strives in its establishment, fulfillment, and revival; the working and striving for it is among the most excellent of deeds, because it revives a sunnah.

And indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever establishes a good sunnah shall have its reward and the reward of those who act upon it until the Day of Judgment, without anything being diminished from their rewards.

key_terms.إحياء السنة: Reviving the sunnah — reinstating forgotten or neglected prophetic practices
key_terms.الجهاد: jihad — here used in its broadest sense encompassing inner spiritual struggle, communal defense, and revival of religious practice
key_terms.سنة: sunnah — prophetic practice or recommended deed; in this hadith distinguished from obligatory as a separate category
key_terms.مجاهدة النفس: Striving against the soul — inner jihad, self-discipline from sinful desires

ai.seo_question: What are the four kinds of jihad according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) responds to a question from Fudayl ibn Iyad — a famous ascetic of the early Islamic period — by presenting a comprehensive taxonomy of jihad into four types: two obligatory (self-discipline against sin, and defense against near enemies) and two forms of sunnah (collective armed defense with the Imam's leadership, and personal striving to revive prophetic practices). The Imam then cites a hadith of the Prophet establishing that reviving good practices earns perpetual reward. This classification reflects the Shia jurisprudential framework where offensive jihad requires the presence of an infallible Imam, while internal jihad against the ego is considered the greatest struggle.
